conceptual assets.information: The 32-bit clock-frequency value reported by the system-information register is initialized from CLOCK_FREQUENCY and can be replaced by a bus write; software depends on it for the system-information read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is not required by the RTL's use because the value is ordinary system information returned on bus_rsp_o.data at line 168. Integrity is at risk because an unchecked bus write selected by the conditions at line 94 stores bus_req_i.data into sysinfo(0) at line 95. Availability is not implicated because the value does not gate or block any required transfer; the response logic only reads it at line 168. No privileged, override, bypass or test behavior acts on this value; only the normal bus-write condition at line 94 controls modification.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write to the clock-frequency register can replace the reported value and cause software relying on system information to use incorrect timing.

considered, not kept.concept: Static hardware capability and configuration metadata
considered, not kept.reason: The build-time-values rule bars this information as a conceptual asset because sysinfo(1) through sysinfo(3) are generated solely from generics and constants and cannot be changed at run time, despite being returned at lines 102-150 and 168.

Access-command fields are part of the access they perform, while buf_ack only repeats the request strobe and buf_adr only holds the access address during service, as shown at lines 160-162 and 168-170, so they are not information pieces of their own.

reply keys: the 2026-10-13 format as written in 'raw'; 'reply' holds it in v5 keys
